reason: Book is working and nothing material has broken the thesis. NAV is +4.62% since 2026-07-17 vs SPY +2.37%, max drawdown a shallow -2.89%, and none of the ten wide-moat/high-ROIC names show a thesis-breaking event on a fresh check today (2026-09-15): MSFT ($500.90, steady Azure/AI momentum, in-line Q4 FY26 beat), GOOGL ($344.82, no fresh antitrust escalation found, AI capex read as a positive not a risk), LLY ($1,147, Berenberg upgrade to $1,400 PT on obesity-drug leadership), AVGO ($343.95, ~flat YTD, only a sentiment wobble on AI-demand-pace debate, no fundamental break) all look intact. The one real flag is ORCL: down to ~$141 (below the packet's $144.20 mark) on restructuring costs, a 13% workforce reduction, and a widely reported $40B debt-funded AI-capex financing plan raising leverage concerns -- a legitimate risk to monitor, but it's only a 9% equal-weight sleeve with an existing -18% stop already attached, and the point of an equal-weight ten-name compounder basket is that no single leg should force a book-wide rebuild. On the FOMC: I used investing.com's Fed Rate Monitor tool (live CME-fed-funds-futures-derived) for the 2026-09-16 decision, which showed 90.1% probability of a hold at 3.75-4.00% and only 9.9% for a 25bp cut, with 0% priced for 50bp -- i.e. markets are leaning toward no cut, though I could not get a second independent source (CME FedWatch itself returned 503, MarketWatch/Reuters were blocked) to corroborate that 90/10 split, so I'm flagging real single-source uncertainty here rather than presenting it as consensus -- other desks reading the same futures curve differently is plausible given how thin my cross-check was. Regardless of which way the meeting breaks, this is a long-only, unlevered quality-compounder book, not a rates-timing trade: a hold is a mild negative for duration-sensitive growth multiples but these are cash-generative moat businesses that don't live or die on one 25bp decision, and a surprise cut would if anything be a tailwind for the same names I already own. Given no leg has broken its underlying quality/moat thesis, the stops are already doing the risk-management job on the one softer name (ORCL), and a full or partial replacement would burn real transaction costs (2bps/side equities, plus any leveraged-ETF or spread costs) chasing a coin-flip-odds macro event the book isn't designed to time, holding is the higher-expected-value choice over trading into FOMC day.
